subject: Swift Retail onboarding: throughput & tail-latency run coordination
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rios <elena@swiftretail.com>, Tom Anders <tom.anders@swiftretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Swift Retail onboarding: throughput & tail-latency run coordination

Hi Elena + Tom,

Congrats on hitting the pre-onboard milestone — excited to get the first performance runs scheduled. I want to line up a short plan so the Redwood runtime and your SREs run against the same assumptions. Proposed high-level targets we discussed internally:

- Steady-state throughput: 1,200 requests/sec (sustained for 30m window)
- Warmup window: 10–15 minutes with increasing concurrency
- P95 latency target: <= 120 ms (in-region)
- P99 tail target: <= 350 ms (we'll measure across 95/99/99.9)
- Error budget: < 0.5% request errors during steady-state

Can you confirm the typical session shape and token distributions so Monica can tune the KV-warm cache behavior? Attachments: I attached a short CSV with our suggested request mixes and a checklist for onboarding artifacts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica to share the concrete load plan and exact endpoint/headers.
2) We pick a 2-hour slot next week for a baseline run + a failover run.
3) We share the run results template and sync within 24 hours for remediation actions.

If this looks okay, Monica and Tessa will take this to scheduling and pick proposed slots.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs):
- swift-retail-load-plan.csv (CSV, request mix + concurrency steps)
- redwood-onboard-checklist.pdf (PDF, pre-run artifacts)

From: Elena Rios <elena@swiftretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Swift Retail onboarding: throughput & tail-latency run coordination

Thanks Ben — this is a helpful summary. Quick clarifications from our side before Monica builds the run script:

- Our expected steady-state concurrency is roughly 350 concurrent sessions; typical request size distribution is 60% single-turn short prompts (~20 tokens), 30% multi-turn chat (~120 tokens total), 10% embeddings/rerank calls.
- We run in us-west-2 with a mixed fleet (some warm instances with local cache).
- Can you confirm whether Redwood will do prefix/KV cache pre-warm for the multi-turn flows, or if we should seed them from replay?

We prefer the run window during our SRE overlap next Tue/Wed afternoon PST. Also, procurement asked for a short note they can attach to the PO about the acceptance criteria — can you include the p95/p99 thresholds in a single-line summary?

Thanks,
Elena Rios
Head of Platform Operations
Swift Retail

On 11/22/26 09:15, Ben Carter wrote:
> Congrats on hitting the pre-onboard milestone — excited to get the first performance runs scheduled. ...

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rios <elena@swiftretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Swift Retail onboarding: throughput & tail-latency run coordination

Hi Elena — thanks for the shapes and environment info. We'll handle KV/prefix warm as part of the Redwood-run; two notes below plus an attached run template.

Planned run details (detailed):
- Environment: us-west-2 (customer VPC peering to Redwood dedicated cluster)
- Endpoints: /generate (text), /chat (multi-turn), /embed (vector) — we'll provide exact headers and a signed test token.
- Request mix (per your numbers): 60/30/10 mapped to our generator and embed harness.
- Concurrency profile: ramp 0 -> 350 over 10 minutes, hold for 30 minutes (steady-state), then ramp-down; repeat once for failover with degraded instance set.
- Warm/caching: We'll run a 15-minute seed phase that replays representative multi-turn contexts to populate KV caches; no manual seeding required from your side unless you prefer identical traces.
- Metrics to capture: P50/P95/P99/P99.9 latencies, server-side queue depth, GPU utilization, token/sec, request error codes, and end-to-end tail spikes (99.99).
- Acceptance criteria short line for procurement: "Acceptance: P95 <= 120 ms, P99 <= 350 ms, steady-state throughput >= 1200 req/s, error rate < 0.5%"

Attachments (stubs):
- run-results-template.xlsx (XLSX, columns for latency buckets + environment tags)
- swift-retail-load-plan.csv (the request mix you saw)

Operational notes:
- We'll produce a single JSON artifact with raw time-series and a short summary PDF within 4 hours of run completion.
- If we see p99 spikes > 350 ms, we'll triage for cache/memory pressure and propose two mitigation knobs: (1) increase batch size threshold for throughput-sensitive paths, or (2) pin a dedicated smaller-quantized variant for latency-critical routes. We'll note remediation steps in the run report.

Proposed slots (PST):
- Tue 2026-11-30 14:00–16:00
- Wed 2026-12-01 13:00–15:00

Ben/Tessa: please confirm one slot and whether you want us to run a dry-run the day before (30-min smoke).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success — Performance Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rios <elena@swiftretail.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T10:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Swift Retail onboarding: throughput & tail-latency run coordination

Elena — thanks for the quick clarifications. We have penciled in Wed 2026-12-01 13:00–15:00 PST for the full baseline + failover run, plus Tue 2026-11-30 13:30–14:00 PST for a 30-minute smoke dry-run.

Checklist for the dry-run (quick):
- A test token will be emailed to your SRE alias.
- Confirm VPC peering endpoint and any IP allowlist entries to our test subnet.
- Provide one representative multi-turn trace (if you want identical cache seeding).

I'll create a calendar invite and share the Drive folder (link below) with run artifacts and the results template. We will also include a short executive one-liner for procurement in the invite description.

Calendar invites + Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_swiftrun

Thanks — see you next week,
Tessa Morgan
Onboarding Ops Lead
Redwood Inference
